metadata.title: feat: implement hierarchical plugin condition evaluation
metadata.author: ja8zyjits

description:
# ✨ Feature / Enhancement PR

## 🔗 Epic / Issue
Closes #3930

---

## 🚀 Summary
Implements hierarchical plugin condition evaluation with hybrid AND/OR logic, replacing the previous OR-only evaluation. Within each condition object, all fields must match (AND logic), while multiple condition objects use OR logic, enabling precise control over plugin execution contexts.

---

## 🧪 Checks

- [x] `make lint` passes
- [x] `make test` passes
- [x] CHANGELOG updated (if user-facing)

---

## 📓 Notes

### Breaking Change

**⚠️ This is a breaking change.** The plugin condition evaluation logic has been fundamentally changed from OR-based to hybrid AND/OR-based evaluation.

**Impact:**
- Existing plugin configurations with multiple conditions will execute differently
- Same YAML configuration produces different runtime behavior
- Requires configuration review and testing before upgrade

**Migration Required:**
- Review all plugin configurations with multiple conditions
- Restructure conditions to use hybrid AND/OR semantics
- Test thoroughly in non-production environments

### Architecture Changes

**New Evaluation Logic:**
```
Within condition object: ALL fields must match (AND)
Across condition objects: ANY object can match (OR)
```

This enables expressions like:
```yaml
# (tenant=healthcare AND tool=patient_reader) OR (server=prod AND user=admin_*)
conditions:
  - tenant_ids: ["healthcare"]
    tools: ["patient_reader"]
  - server_ids: ["prod"]
    user_patterns: ["admin_.*"]
```

**Evaluation Flow:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Plugin Conditions List] --> B[Condition Object 1]
    A --> C[Condition Object 2]
    
    B --> B1{All Fields Match?}
    B1 -->|Yes| E[Execute Plugin]
    B1 -->|No| F[Try Next Object]
    
    C --> C1{All Fields Match?}
    C1 -->|Yes| E
    C1 -->|No| G[Skip Plugin]
    
    F --> C
    
    style E fill:#90EE90
    style G fill:#FFB6C1
    style A fill:#E0F2F7,stroke:#4CAF50,stroke-width:3px
```

### Changes Made

1. **Core Logic** (`mcpgateway/plugins/framework/utils.py`):
   - Replaced `payload_matches()` with hybrid AND/OR evaluation
   - Added fail-fast short-circuit optimization
   - Enhanced debug logging for condition evaluation

2. **Tests** (`tests/unit/mcpgateway/plugins/framework/`):
   - Comprehensive test coverage for AND logic within condition objects
   - Tests for OR logic across multiple condition objects
   - Edge cases: empty conditions, single fields, complex scenarios
   - New test file: `test_utils_and_logic.py`

3. **Documentation** (`docs/docs/architecture/plugins.md`):
   - Updated condition evaluation section
   - Added configuration examples
   - Documented evaluation order and short-circuit behavior
   - Migration guide with common patterns

4. **CHANGELOG** (`CHANGELOG.md`):
   - Breaking change notice
   - Feature description
   - Migration guidance reference

### Security Benefits

- **Defense-in-depth**: AND logic enables multi-factor plugin execution control
- **Reduced attack surface**: Eliminates accidental policy bypass via OR logic
- **Clearer intent**: Conditions explicitly state all requirements
- **Enhanced audit trail**: Debug logging shows exact evaluation path

### Performance

- **Fail-fast optimization**: Short-circuits on first non-matching field
- **Expected improvement**: Faster evaluation for non-matching conditions
- **No memory impact**: Same data structures
- **Minimal logging overhead**: Debug logging only when enabled

feat: implement hierarchical plugin condition evaluation

- Add support for AND/OR/NOT logical operators in plugin conditions
- Implement nested condition evaluation with proper precedence
- Add comprehensive test coverage for condition logic
- Update documentation with examples and migration guide

BREAKING CHANGE: Plugin condition syntax now supports hierarchical
evaluation. Simple string conditions are still supported but complex
conditions require new AND/OR/NOT structure.
